text: Right, so the plan for Saturday. I've got the list here somewhere.
Is it the same list as last time? Because half of that never got done.
Mostly the same. The hedge, the bins, the bit of fence by the gate, and the compost.
The compost is the big one. It's been sitting there since the spring.
Okay, so the hedge first. What I thought we could do is cut it right back on the street side, and then on the garden side we could take it down to about shoulder height and
Sorry, can I stop you there? The hedge isn't ours. It belongs to the house at the end of the row.
Is that right?
I'm fairly sure. They trimmed it themselves the year before last.
Then we should ask them before anyone touches it.
Fine. The hedge is off the list until we ask. Bins next.
The bins just need moving round the side so the lid stops blowing open.
That's ten minutes. Then the fence by the gate.
Somebody will need the long ladder for the top rail.
Who actually has the key to the shed where the ladder lives?
Nobody? Wonderful.
I think it was left under the blue pot by the back step.
I'll look tonight. Now, the compost. You said it's the big one.

It is. The way it works is this. There are three bays. The left one is where everything new goes, the peelings and the grass and the cardboard torn up small. When that one is full you fork the whole lot across into the middle bay, which turns it and lets the air in, and that's the part that makes it heat up. Then after a couple of months the middle goes across into the right hand bay to finish, and by the summer the right hand bay is dark and crumbly and you can spread it on the beds. The trouble is nobody has turned anything since the spring, so the left bay is overflowing and the middle one has gone cold and wet.
So that's a whole morning on its own.
At least a morning. Two people with forks.
Let me look at the forecast before we promise a whole morning.
Dry until about three, then rain.
Then compost first, while it's dry, and the bins and the fence after lunch.
I can bring the wheelbarrow. The tyre is flat but I have a pump.
Good. I'll bring gloves and the big bags for the hedge, if we ever get to the hedge.
We won't.
No, probably not.
What time are we starting?
Nine? Half nine?
Half nine. Nobody will be out of bed at nine on a Saturday.
Half nine at the gate then. And someone remind me to bring the pump, because I will forget the pump.
I'll put a note through your door on Friday.
Right. Hedge on hold, compost first, bins and fence after lunch, and the ladder key under the blue pot, maybe.
Maybe.
Sounds like a plan.
